Reference audit and coverage

Independent fictional demo based on the project conversation, ten-page deck, mind map and 45 sampled frames across the supplied reference video. This was not a full audio transcription.

Audit finding

The latest reported assignment asks for workflows and code. Earlier advice that a presentation alone was sufficient was speculative. Both are included here.

Observed evidence

Lead editing around 8:30; RNR and authorized transfers around 14:05–14:15; Not Interested and Lost around 14:25–14:30; intake around 18:40; Settings around 19:45 onward. Visible status names, menus and options informed this interface.

Implemented

Leads, Sellers, Data, Process, Notice Board, Channel Partners, Admin, Marketing, HR, Sales, Digital, Settings, Knowledge, Inventory, Reports, Follow Ups and Search. Forms save session records. Imports and bulk changes validate before commit. Related dropdowns use current users and projects.

Reconstructed behavior

D1–D4 are dashboard shortcuts, not four days. Detailed dashboard content and supporting-module rules, SVS/SVD details, round-robin assignment, one open task, transaction boundaries, role guards and duplicate checks are demo implementations, not verified ClientFirst parity. RNR retains status until attempt four; retry dates are entered manually.

Boundaries

Refresh resets changes. No backend, login, production authorization or live CRM integration. Messages are local drafts; builder registrations are local records. Cost-sheet rates are entered by the user. No actual financial or external action occurs.

Walkthrough

Add lead → edit and Verify → schedule/complete visit → follow up → transfer → Book. Separately show RNR, Not Interested / Lost Lead, source conversion, CSV import preview, bulk update preview, supporting forms and reports. Inspect the workflow code from this page.
